findings.place: tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js: findIsPlaceholder (lines 533-560: the tests `starts with your` and `contains example`), used by findValue (unquoted line 749 and quoted line 734) and by findUrlPassword (line 805)
findings.item: Q7 (and decisions/0102 items 14 and 18: no narrowing of the old rules except the named ones)
findings.what: The two substring tests of the placeholder class are applied to the whole value up to the next white space, comma, semicolon or quote. A real-looking secret with anything glued behind it that contains the word example (or a glued value that starts with your) is therefore kept as a placeholder, and the old rules M2, M8, M9 hid every one of these. Realistic shapes: a query string with a secret followed by a redirect to https://example.com/..., a user:secret@example.com address inside a value, `Authorization: Basic <base64>&x=example`, `Bearer <token>&redirect=example.com`, and a quoted `password: "<secret> for example.com"`. It is not the named residual (4) (a secret written exactly like a placeholder) and not (6) (text after the first value): the first value here is the secret itself.
findings.evidence: Own runs on a copy outside the project with the old rules (scratch copy of the base tag with the rules exported) and findSecrets side by side: of 23 glued variants in one run 19 print KEEP for the new check, every one of them hidden by the old rules, and every shape named above is among the 19; the shape `token=<12 letters and digits>&redirect=https://example.com/cb` is kept, the same text with a space, a comma or a semicolon instead of the glue character is refused. An independent reference written from the requirement text agrees with the code on every case (0 disagreements in 4.3 million strings), so this is a gap in the rule itself, not a slip in the code. Same cause makes a kept call-class value swallow a glued pair: `token=f(x)&<name>=<literal>` is kept (old M9 hid it).
findings.fix: Apply the `your` prefix and the `example` substring tests only to a value made of word characters [A-Za-z0-9_.-] (the shape of every placeholder in the requirement: YOUR_API_KEY, pw-example, example9, your-token); any value with another character (`&`, `/`, `:`, `@`, a space) is a literal and is refused. Same restriction for the quoted content and for the address password. Add refuse samples (the shapes above) and keep samples (pw-example, YOUR_API_KEY, example9) to the design table and the test, and name in the README that a kept call-class value is not scanned inside. This changes a rule of REQ-102 (class З): it needs the micro-amendment gate (REQ-VALIDATOR) before CODE-FIXER, and it makes the check stricter, not looser. After the fix this role runs again.

findings.what: The README names residual risks (1)-(4) and (6) but not the two old holes of (5): an assignment with a space before the sign (`password = "..."`) and an address with no user (`redis://:<secret>@host`); both are kept by the new check as they were by the old one (parity table below). The paragraph also says a name the journal rules would change is counted in «и ещё N», but when it is the only refused file nothing is named and no count is printed (the constant text only; checked with secretDetail).
findings.evidence: bypass table: `password = <value>` keep/old-kept; `redis://:<value>@db` keep/old-kept; secretDetail(["t-0001-1-app.test.js"]) prints the constant text.
findings.fix: Add the two forms to the residual-risk sentence and say that the count is shown only beside at least one named file.

findings.place: tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js FIND_PREFIXED (line 815, three look-behind regexes with an unbounded repeat) and tools/src/team/runner.js depsOf (line 118-141)
findings.what: The prefixed-key regexes throw RangeError (backtrack stack) on a single key-shaped run longer than about 5.33 MiB (5 593 088 characters). Every path that reaches findSecrets through #publish or acceptResult is held to 5 MiB first, so the headroom is 6 percent; but depsOf reads a stored file without a size check, so a file put into files/ by hand that is larger than that makes depsOf throw a non-TeamError, against the code comment `nothing is thrown`. The old code with maskSecrets threw the same, so it is not a regression.
findings.evidence: bisect run: threshold 5 593 088 for sk-, ghp_, github_pat_ and repeated sk-; at exactly 5 MiB all four print F4/F5; depsOf on a 10 MiB hand-placed file printed `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` (old maskSecrets: same message).
findings.fix: Either skip the content check by a try/catch that turns a RangeError into the withheld text in depsOf, or bound the repeat ({16,4096} is enough to decide the form); state the dependence on FILE_BYTES_MAX in a code comment.
